data.name: Vishal
data.gender_notes: Vishal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘vish’ meaning ‘to conquer’. In Hindu mythology, Vishal is an epithet of various deities, particularly Lord Vishnu, signifying power, strength, and fearlessness. The name Vishal carries the meaning “Brave, Valiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vishal usually hope their child will grow to embody brave, valiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblematic of courage and resilience in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Vishal belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brave, Valiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vishal total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vishal holds great significance in Hindu culture. It is revered as an attribute of various gods, especially Lord Vishnu, who is known as the preserver and protector of the universe. The name conjures images of power, might, and triumph, echoing the spiritual qualities associated with it.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Vishal has deep spiritual significance, representing the inability to be defeated or overcome by negativity, fear, or doubt. It symbolizes strength, courage, and resilience in the face of adversity. The name also symbolizes freedom from possessiveness and arrogance, reminding one to be humble and charitable. Ultimately, the name Vishal encapsulates the Hindu ideal of living a courageous and virtuous life, embracing challenges with grace and unwavering determination.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vishal means expansive, vast, and broad in the Hindu context, symbolizing the limitless nature of the Divine or the individual soul.

vedic_reference.note: Vishal is a Sanskrit name derived from the root word 'vis' meaning 'to spread'. In Hindu mythology, Vishal is a synonym for Vishnu and also refers to the expansive, all-pervading aspect of the universe.

historical_references.reference: According to the Mahabharata, Vishal was a king of the Haihayas who ruled over Mathura. He was a grandson of the legendary king, Yadu, and the father of King Shatadhanva. Vishal is also known for a significant battle fought between him and the Pandavas, where he was defeated.

Another reference to Vishal can be found in the Puranic texts, where he is described as an incarnation of Vishnu and is venerated in various temples across India. In this context, Vishal symbolizes the expansive nature of the divine.
